findings.title: Slots inside a date override bypass all busy-time checks
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot is on a date-override day and is not detected as outside the override, dateOverrideExist is true and the function immediately returns true. It never reaches the busy.every(...) check at the end, so calendar events and accepted Cal bookings overlapping that slot are ignored for fixed and round-robin hosts on override days, allowing double-booking.

findings.title: Date-override check mishandles multiple and partially-overlapping overrides
findings.body: The dateOverrides.find callback returns true as soon as a slot is outside one override on that day, even if the slot is inside a second override the same day (e.g. split availability 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00), so valid slots are rejected. Conversely it only tests slotStartTime.isAfter(override end), not slotEndTime, so a slot starting inside an override but ending after it (17:30 for 60 minutes with an override ending 18:00) is treated as inside and made bookable.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects split shifts and allows non-working days
findings.body: The workingHours.find callback returns true when the slot is outside ANY one working-hour entry, so with split hours on a day (09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) every slot is outside at least one entry and gets rejected. If no entry includes slotStartTime.day() at all, find returns nothing and execution falls through to the busy check, treating a non-working day as available. Additionally lines 141-142 compute both start and end from slotStartTime, so a slot starting before closing time but ending after workingHours.endTime is never rejected.

findings.title: Empty date-override comparison uses Dayjs object identity
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference and is always false, so the intended detection of a zero-length override (start equals end, meaning unavailable) never triggers. A slot exactly at the shifted start of such an override then falls through, sets dateOverrideExist, and is returned as available.

findings.title: Converted overrides lose day shifts when the invitee-local time crosses midnight
findings.body: The override conversion extracts only hour()*60+minute() from the offset-shifted start and end, discarding any date change. For example an organizer override ending after midnight in the invitee timezone yields an endTime smaller than startTime (e.g. 20:30-00:30 becomes 1230-30), and buildSlots skips boundaries where start >= end; because the user's normal working hours were already removed for that override, the user incorrectly shows no availability instead of the evening portion, and overrides shifted to the previous/next invitee day are placed on the wrong day.

findings.title: Optional override timeZone is used without a fallback
findings.body: TimeRange.timeZone is optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts, but getSlots unconditionally calls dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone). Callers that supply dateOverrides without timeZone (permitted by the type, and the pre-existing shape) will have the organizer offset computed against the system/default timezone instead of the organizerTimeZone already passed into getSlots, producing wrongly shifted override slots rather than falling back to organizerTimeZone.

findings.title: No test covers the claimed round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
findings.body: The only added test queries a single-user event in a second timezone and asserts the same UTC slots. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, a fixed host with a date override and a loose host, nor a busy booking on an override day, so the new checkIfIsAvailable dateOverride/workingHours filtering for fixed and loose hosts - the main behaviour this PR claims to fix - is untested and regressions such as busy times being ignored on override days would not be caught.
